title: Query Results runner added param_query_N_{k=v} syntax that substitutes user-supplied values verbatim into another data source's SQL, bypassing Redash's parameter validation and view-only safety check.

vulnerable_findings.explanation: The PR adds a new parameterized-query path (extract_query_params, replace_query_parameters, and the new query_params loop in create_tables_from_query_ids) that executes a referenced query with user-supplied parameters. findings.explanation: The PR adds a new parameterized-query path (extract_query_params, replace_query_parameters, and the new query_params loop in create_tables_from_query_ids) that executes a referenced query with user-supplied parameters. The authorization check in _load_query (lines 43-54) only verifies the requester's access to the query's data_source (has_access(query.data_source, user, view_only)) and org membership. It does NOT verify that the requester is allowed to access the referenced query object itself (e.g. via require_permission_or_owner / has_permission_or_owner on query.user_id, or a query-level group check). This is inconsistent with the rest of the codebase, where query access is gated by ownership or group permissions (see redash/permissions.py require_permission_or_owner, is_admin_or_owner). As a result, a user who has view access to the data source can read the results of any query in the same org by referencing its id (query_<id> / param_query_<id>), even if they are not the owner and not in a group granted access to that specific query — an IDOR / incorrect-authorization exposure of query results.

evidence.content:
def create_tables_from_query_ids(user, connection, query_ids, query_params, cached_query_ids=[]):
    for query_id in set(cached_query_ids):
        results = get_query_results(user, query_id, True)
        table_name = "cached_query_{query_id}".format(query_id=query_id)
        create_table(connection, table_name, results)

    for query in set(query_params):
        results = get_query_results(user, query[0], False, query[1])
        table_hash = hashlib.md5("query_{query}_{hash}".format(query=query[0], hash=query[1]).encode()).hexdigest()
        table_name = "query_{query_id}_{param_hash}".format(query_id=query[0], param_hash=table_hash)
        create_table(connection, table_name, results)

    for query_id in set(query_ids):
        results = get_query_results(user, query_id, False)
        table_name = "query_{query_id}".format(query_id=query_id)
        create_table(connection, table_name, results)

findings.suggested_fix: In _load_query, in addition to the data_source check, verify the requester is allowed to access the specific query object: check ownership (query.user_id == user.id) or admin permission, or a query-level group permission (e.g. user.has_access(query, ACCESS_TYPE_VIEW)), and raise PermissionError otherwise. This matches the require_permission_or_owner / is_admin_or_owner pattern used elsewhere in redash/permissions.py.
